newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UBS private bank unit charged on Jersey.
newsitem.headline: UBS private bank unit charged on Jersey.

text.p: Cantrade Privatbank AG, wholly owned by Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS), on Tueday said Jersey police had charged Cantrade and one its officers under the Investors (Prevention of Fraud) Jersey Law.
"The charges against the bank are being investigated and subject to the investigation will be contested," Zurich-based Cantrade said in a statement.
"A plea of not guilty will be entered at the appropriate time," it added.
A Cantrade spokesman was not immediately available to elaborate on the charges.
The bank said the charges were in addition to a related civil law action against Cantrade that has been pending for some time.
Cantrade said the management team of subsidiary Cantrade Jersey had been changed since the alleged offences took place between 1988 and 1993.
"The officer charged has been suspended pending the resolution of the charges against him," it said.

The Cantrade Privatbank Group comprises Cantrade Privatbank of Zurich and subsidiaries in Geneva, Lugano and Jersey. It posted a group net profit of 73.1 million Swiss francs in 1995 and cash flow of 140.7 million.
Cantrade said the earlier civil action was brought by investment managers of funds used for foreign exchange trading.
"The trader concerned, Robert Young, who was charged in August, is not and has never been an employee of Cantrade," the bank said.
It said Young had been trading pursuant to a mandate given by the investment managers.
"Cantrade is defending the civil action but will meet any claims which are legally justified," it said.
Cantrade said it was treating these matter extremely seriously and was committed to complying with all relevant laws and standards of best practice.
"The bank is sound, well-capitalised and will meet all its obligations as they fall due," the statement said.
